# Ecliptic Launcher · Beta 9

Customize Home, manage your installations from the Library, and use Friends to get into Minecraft together.

## Home and Library

- Cherry Waterline is the new Ecliptic Night backdrop, with moonlight across the lake. Use your own image or video, adjust its colour, and save appearance profiles.
- Move or resize Home widgets and pose your player directly in the model preview. Minecraft news and Ecliptic release notes are available from **News & updates**.
- Click a Library card to open its installation. The three-dot menu gives you its actions, and deleting an installation asks for confirmation before removing its managed files, including its worlds and mods.
- Launch multiple installations in separate game folders and see the running count in the titlebar. The Home Play button shows launch progress.

## Friends and servers

- Open Friends for requests, recently played players, profiles, and invitation history. Invite a friend to a joined or hosted server and choose a compatible installation when joining.
- Try singleplayer invitations by opening your world to LAN and entering Minecraft’s port in Friends. This experimental Windows flow uses a linked ngrok account with TCP access. World cards use the save’s thumbnail when available.
- Join Grind MC from Public Servers, or manage local servers with server cards, player controls, and world views.

## Updates and fixes

- Review linked modpack and individual mod updates from your installation.
- Library, Addons, and installation pages give more space to scrolling content. Selecting a day in Digital Wellbeing keeps the chart’s date range in place.

## Before testing

This is a Windows x64 beta. Existing beta users can use the in-launcher updater. New users should download **Ecliptic-Setup.exe**. Back up worlds you want to keep before deleting an installation. The singleplayer invite flow has been checked in a test fixture. A real two-player join remains a beta test case.
